newsitem.title: USA: Neoprobe device gets FDA clearance.
newsitem.headline: Neoprobe device gets FDA clearance.

text.p: Neoprobe Corp, a maker of cancer detection products, said on Monday that its hand-held gamma-detecting probe, the Neoprobe 1500 Portable Radioisotope Detector, received marketing clearance from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration and will be launched next month.

Neoprobe's 1500 Portable Radioisotope Detector, which was developed in collaboration with United States Surgical Corp, has enhanced features for mapping lymphatic systems to evaluate the spread of cancers, the company said.
Also, Neoprobe said in a statement that European officials requested more manufacturing testing data for its RIGScan CR49 device.

Neoprobe said the product is still on track for regulators to rule on the marketing this year in the United States and Europe for RIGScan CR49 for detecting metastatic colorectal cancer. The company applied to the FDA for a compassionate use program of the device, it said.
The company said it also plans to study product indications on the RIGScan CR49 with adenocarcinomas, including pancreatic, stomach, ovarian and endometrial cancers in a Phase II trial.

Also, Neoprobe expects to conclude negotiations on study design with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in late summer in order to file an Investigational New Drug application for the company's multicenter Phase II clinical trial for RIGS/ACT for colorectal cancer, the company said.
Neoprobe is also co-developing laparoscopic products with U.S. Surgical for minimally invasive evaluation of colorectal cancer.
All of the clinical trials and the compassionate use program are expected to begin by the fourth quarter this year.
